body:
**Adversarial review, round 1** on `718f090` by claude-opus-5-5 (builder: claude-sonnet-5-5).

No blocking findings. FR-007: both the /latest and /history lookups go through the shared `find` helper, which uses `Object.hasOwn`. That means `__proto__`, `constructor`, `toString` and other prototype names return 404 unknown_sensor. Percent-encoded IDs stay encoded in `URL.pathname`, so they can't get around the check, and there are no other `readings[...]` lookups in server.ts. FR-001/002: filtering uses inclusive `>=`/`<=`. Results come out oldest first because the fixed data in data.ts is generated in ascending order and filter keeps that order. FR-003: the unknown-sensor check runs first and returns 404 unknown_sensor. FR-004: the check is `to - from > 7d` (strict), so exactly 7 days gives 200 and 7d+1s gives 400. FR-005: an empty window returns 200 with `readings: []`. FR-006: openapi.yaml already documents /history with the History schema, the 400 and the 404. The response shape matches the History schema: entries are `{at, value}`, with `sensorId` from the path. Malformed or missing from/to evaluate to NaN and return 200 with an empty array; the spec explicitly puts this out of scope. The cases are real tests. They check exact timestamps, the 25-reading day, the 169-reading 7-day boundary, separation between sensors, and five prototype IDs on both endpoints. The change stays inside server.ts.



Only @dharishan04 can close a finding without a fix: `/dismiss <F-n> <reason>`.
